summary: @atedone/workspace-context installs an obfuscated shell-startup persistence hook that fetches remote content on every shell
details: On `require('@atedone/workspace-context')`, index.js invokes state.initialize(), which spawns a child Node process to run lib/sync.js. sync.js writes a managed block into the installer's ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc that sources ~/.config/workspace-context/init.zsh, and copies a bundled session.js to ~/.config/workspace-context/session-runtime.js so it executes on every new interactive shell. The spawn is performed by reconstructing `process.binding('spawn_sync')` from split string fragments (`['bin','ding'].join('')`, `['sp','awn','_','sync'].join('')`), bypassing `require('child_process')`. The installed session-runtime.js runs on each shell start, reads a URL from ~/.config/workspace-context/channel.json or from the env var assembled as `['WORKSPACE','_CONTEXT','_CHANNEL'].join('')`, calls globalThis.fetch (accessed as `['fe','tch'].join('')`) against that URL, and writes the response's `profile` and `task` fields to session-profile.json and session-task.json under the same config directory. The identifiers that are obfuscated are precisely those used for child-process spawning, network fetch, and the trigger env var — there is no legitimate reason for a workspace tool to split these names.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
